candidates.original_title: Knowledge Transfers from Multinational to Domestic Firms: Evidence from Worker Mobility
candidates.description: When workers leave multinationals and are rehired at domestic establishments, the wages of their new coworkers who have already been present in the establishment increase (replicated for Norway).
candidates.citation_sentence: This paper replicates Poole (2013) using comprehensive Norwegian and Irish register data.
candidates.notes: [ling26: no entry matched this anchor] Paper classifies itself as robustness-extension replication type. Norway uses comprehensive register data covering all private-sector workers 1996-2007. Main spillover effect (γ_M - γ_D) is significant and positive.

candidates.original_title: Knowledge Transfers from Multinational to Domestic Firms: Evidence from Worker Mobility
candidates.description: When workers leave multinationals and are rehired at domestic establishments, the wages of their new coworkers who have already been present in the establishment increase (replicated for Ireland, 2005-2010).
candidates.citation_sentence: This paper replicates Poole (2013) using comprehensive Norwegian and Irish register data.
candidates.notes: Norway replication of Poole (2013); main effect of multinational wage spillovers confirmed; uses comprehensive register data covering all private-sector workers rather than a 1% sample. Ireland 2005-2010 sample period. Main spillover effect (γ_M - γ_D) is significant and positive. Ireland split into two time periods for comparability with the original 6-year Brazil sample.

candidates.original_title: Knowledge Transfers from Multinational to Domestic Firms: Evidence from Worker Mobility
candidates.description: When workers leave multinationals and are rehired at domestic establishments, the wages of their new coworkers who have already been present in the establishment increase (replicated for Ireland, 2011-2016).
candidates.citation_sentence: This paper replicates Poole (2013) using comprehensive Norwegian and Irish register data.
candidates.notes: Ireland replication of Poole (2013); main effect confirmed across both 2005-2010 and 2011-2016 periods; uses firm-level administrative data covering all formal workers. Ireland 2011-2016 sample period. Main spillover effect (γ_M - γ_D) is significant and positive. Heterogeneity analyses across unionisation, skill intensity, job tenure, and wages are mostly not statistically significant for any country, which the authors note as a divergence from the original.

candidates.original_title: Knowledge Transfers from Multinational to Domestic Firms: Evidence from Worker Mobility
candidates.description: Norwegian matched employer-employee data replicate the claim that when workers leave multinational firms and are rehired by domestic establishments, the wages of incumbent domestic coworkers increase.
candidates.citation_sentence: As in Poole's 2013 original paper, we employ matched employer-employee data from Ireland and Norway.
candidates.notes: This entry covers the Norway sample. The paper describes the exercise as a robustness-extension replication conducted in a different country and time period from the original Brazilian study.

candidates.original_title: Knowledge Transfers from Multinational to Domestic Firms: Evidence from Worker Mobility
candidates.description: Irish matched employer-employee data from 2005 to 2010 replicate the claim that when workers leave multinational firms and are rehired by domestic firms, the wages of incumbent domestic coworkers increase.
candidates.citation_sentence: As in Poole's 2013 original paper, we employ matched employer-employee data from Ireland and Norway.
candidates.notes: This entry covers the Ireland 2005–2010 sample. The paper reports a positive and statistically significant multinational wage-spillover estimate.

candidates.notes: This entry covers the Ireland 2011–2016 sample. The paper reports a positive and statistically significant multinational wage-spillover estimate.
